Order

.  This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act has been filed by the appellant/Insurance Company arising out of the award dated 31.08.2015 passed by the First Additional, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (hereinafter referred to as "the Claims Tribunal"),
District Gwalior (M.P.) in Claim Case No.84/2014, on the ground of reduction of compensation.
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute.
The findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are also not under challenge.

3. As per the findings of the Claims Tribunal, in the case of death of Murari Lal due to a motor accident, compensation to the tune of Rs.6,64,600/- along with interest from the date of filing of the claim application till its realization has been awarded.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company submitted that NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:4795 2 MA-1163-2015 the impugned award is contrary to the settled principles of law as well as the material available on record.
It is contended that the learned Claims Tribunal has erred in awarding compensation on the higher side.

The claim petition was filed by the claimants under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, however, the learned Claims Tribunal did not National Insurance Company Ltd. Thr. vs Smt. Manju Batham on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176556956/
1 determine the compensation in accordance with Schedule II appended to Section 163-A of the Act.

Instead, the Claims Tribunal assessed the compensation by relying upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma and Others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another,
reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, which pertains to claims under Section 166 of the MV Act.

reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is further submitted that where a claim petition is filed under Section 163-A of the MV Act, the multiplier,
multiplicand and other heads of compensation are required to be awarded strictly as per Schedule II of the Act, without deviation.
Hence, it is prayed that the impugned award be modified and the compensation amount be reduced accordingly.
5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondents No.1 to 7 supported the impugned award and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

It was further submitted that although cross-objections were filed on behalf of respondents No.1 to 7 in the form of I.A. No.668/2016, the same are not pressed and are accordingly dismissed as not pressed.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the entire record of the Claims Tribunal.
7.
On perusal of the record, it is not in dispute that the claim petition was filed under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act.

In such cases, compensation is required to be determined strictly in accordance with the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4795 3 MA-1163-2015 structured formula provided under the Second Schedule to the Act.
When a claim is preferred under Section 163-A, the principles laid down in Sarla Verma (supra), which pertain to claims under Section 166 of the Act, are not applicable.

8. In view of the above, this Court is of the considered opinion that the Claims Tribunal committed a legal error in assessing the compensation by applying the principles laid down in Sarla Verma (supra), which is not permissible in a claim under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act.

9. So far as the income of the deceased is concerned, the Claims Tribunal has rightly assessed the same at Rs.36,000/- per annum, which is in consonance with the income ceiling prescribed under the Second Schedule to Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act.
The said assessment being lawful and justified does not call for any interference by this Court.

10. Accordingly, the compensation is reassessed under the following heads:-
Amount (Rs.) Head 36,000/- per year Income 24,000/- After deducting 1/3rd towards personal expenses (Dependency) 4,32,000/- Multiplier (24,000  18)
9,500/- Other heads (Loss of estate and funeral expenses) 4,41,500/- Total Compensation 11.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.4,41,500/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.6,64,600/-.
Accordingly, the compensation amount is reduced from Rs.6,64,600/- to Rs.4,41,500/-.

All other findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal shall remain undisturbed.
The Insurance Company shall be entitled to refund of the excess amount, if already deposited, in accordance with law.
13. With the aforesaid modification, the appeal stands partly allowed and is disposed of.
